profile.org_note: Homebuilding runs through about 35 local divisions (each under a division president, with its own VP or director of land acquisition) grouped into four geographic operating Areas, West (Chris Edgar), Central (Charlie Tipton), Southeast (Rich McCormick) and North (Tony Barbee), plus a fifth non-geographic Manufacturing/ICG area (Ryan Melin); the 2023, 2024 and 2025 annual reports list the same five area presidents, who sit under COO Matt Koart. The Areas do not match the six SEC reporting segments (Northeast: MD, MA, NJ, PA, RI, VA; Southeast: GA, NC, SC, TN; Florida; Midwest: IL, IN, KY, MI, MN, OH; Texas; West: AZ, CA, CO, NV, NM, OR, UT, WA), and the company does not publish which divisions sit in which Area. There is no published corporate head of land: deals are sourced by division land teams and approved up through area presidents and the COO, with corporate finance (Treasurer Bryce Langen for structured land transactions, SVP Finance David Carrier for asset management) as the land-finance gatekeepers and the Board's Finance and Investment Committee reviewing certain land acquisitions.
profile.summary: Third-largest US homebuilder by the company's own description: 1,014 active communities in 47 markets across 26 states at year-end 2025, selling under Pulte Homes, Centex, Del Webb, DiVosta and John Wieland. It controlled 234,632 lots at 31 Dec 2025, 57% of them under option (133,528 optioned, 101,104 owned), and invested $5.2 billion in land acquisition and development in 2025. Growth moves in the last year are new-market entries run from existing divisions (Cincinnati, Florida Panhandle via a 1,326 to 2,653 homesite contract with St. Joe, Utah).

gaps: Corporate head of land (Chief Land Officer / EVP or SVP Land / national VP land acquisition / chief investment officer): none published on the management page, in the 2023-2025 annual reports' leadership and area-management lists, in the 10-K or proxy, or in any company release 2020-2026; no such role found in trade press in this pass.

Area-to-division mapping: the company names its five area presidents (2025 Annual Report) but does not publish which divisions or states each Area covers. Unassigned in public sources: Georgia (Atlanta / Greenville SC), Houston, San Antonio, Charlotte, Raleigh, Mid-Atlantic, Northeast Corridor, New England, Minnesota, Michigan, Illinois, Northern California, Las Vegas, New Mexico, Pacific Northwest (Michigan and Illinois are linked to the North Area only by inference).

Area-level land and finance heads (Area VP Land / Area VP Finance for West, Central, Southeast, North): not publicly disclosed. Texas franchise-tax officer lists for Pulte Home Company, LLC name several 'Vice President & Asst. Secretary' signatories (2026 report) without function or geography, so they were not added.

Corporate head of land (national VP / SVP of land or chief investment officer): no such title is published. Land sourcing is at division level; corporate land gatekeeping appears to sit in finance (Treasurer Bryce Langen for structured land transactions; SVP Finance David Carrier for asset management). The 10-K refers to homebuilding area presidents and division presidents but does not describe a land approval process.
Area-level land and finance heads (Area VP Land, Area VP Finance for West, Central, Southeast, North): not publicly named in sources reached.

Division land heads: only Houston (Bryan Hahn) and Georgia (Jason Garrett) are confirmed with a 2026 source. Northeast Florida, Arizona and Colorado names are 2022-2023 and tagged Inferred. All other divisions: not found. The company has recently advertised division VP of land acquisition openings (Las Vegas, Dallas-area, Myrtle Beach) per job-board snippets, not confirmed.
Reporting lines: only Todd Sheldon and Kevin Henry are stated as reporting to the CEO. All other lines are inferred from function or from which area president announced an appointment.

Division presidents not confirmed with a current source: New England, Minnesota (last public name Jaime Tharp, 2020), New Mexico (Les Anderson was New Mexico / Colorado president in 2021), Pacific Northwest (Graham Epperson, 2022), Charlotte, Coastal Carolinas, Southeast Florida, Raleigh (Jeff Davis inferred). Another agent is sweeping division presidents.
Robert T. O'Shaughnessy (former CFO) is not listed as a current person: the 2026 proxy says he served as Executive Vice President through 6 March 2026 and he is no longer on the management page.
Treasurer's start date and direct phone / email for land and treasury contacts: not published. Only the IR contact (Jim Zeumer) has a published direct line and email.

Some releases on the company newsroom carry a migration date rather than the original date (the Greenville market-entry release shows March 2026 but describes 2023 openings); dates used here were sanity-checked against release content.

Additional land and finance names: not confirmed. Trade press, local business journals, HBA / ULI pages and county records were not checked; everything here comes from SEC filings and PulteGroup's own sites.
